scoring_justification: The main results (peak PF, ZT, ring energies) are produced by expensive DFT+transport calculations that cannot be repeated in the verifier sandbox. The agent self-reports the computed quantities; the checker compares against the paper's published values with tolerances. This is the strongest feasible tier for this compute-driven paper.

hidden_assets.purpose: Reference peak power factor, ZT, and ring/moat energies from the paper, used as hidden gold for result comparison.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper main figures (Figs. 3,5,7,9) and text descriptions of ring/moat energies.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Values extracted from the paper and verified against the reference solve.sh oracle. The specific values are inline in grading_spec_json.
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: Values are the paper's reported numeric results for the exact same quantities; they are not invented.

outputs.description: Array of objects, one per (material, scattering) pair. Each object reports the peak power factor (peak_pf), peak ZT (peak_zt), and the Fermi level at which they occur. For single quintuple-layer materials, the energies of the inner ring, outer ring, and moat relative to the valence-band edge are additionally provided (may be null for double quintuple-layer materials).

output_contract.notes: The agent must compute scattering parameters so that the average mean free path for backscattering equals 20 nm at the respective band edge. The checker will compare peak_pf against a hidden lower bound (paper value −15%), peak_zt against a hidden lower bound (paper value −10%), and ring/moat energies within ±0.01 eV of hidden references. Relative ordering of PF across scattering models will also be verified.
